thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PG: gpu-pool-eu-west-2 prod queue depth spike - autoscaler errors - paging oncall

pagerbot: Alert details: pool=gpu-pool-eu-west-2, queue=512 -> 4200 in 5m, throttle_rate=50%, autoscaler_errors=AllocationFailed(QuotaExceeded) x120, recent deploy: continuous-batching:v2 rolled out ~22m ago

maya: i’m on it, grabbing logs and checking autoscaler. is there a customer-facing impact yet?

sylvie: seeing increased 5xx from hosted endpoints in eu-west-2 (rate-limited). CS flagged 3 customer complaints in last 10m.

omar: perf dashboards show token latency spiking, tail > 4s for many requests. prefix-cache hitrate dropped from 98% -> 60% around the rollout window.

maya: @ops-sre can you confirm if autoscaler is hitting quota or scale caps?

ops-sre: autoscaler logs show "max_nodes_reached" on several pools and also repeated 429 from cloud provider when requesting GPUs. also AllocationFailed with message "QuotaExceeded: per-account GPU limit".

eng-runtime: confirmed continuous-batching:v2 changed batch_window and kv-prefix ttl; we might be invalidating prefix caches more aggressively. looks like a config: 
```
# rollout config snippet
batching:
  continuous: true
  max_batch_size: 32
  batch_window_ms: 35  # reduced from 80
prefix_cache:
  ttl_ms: 1500  # reduced from 10000
```

eng-runtime: reducing ttl and batch window would increase miss rate and create more short-lived cache entries; combined with higher max_batch_size could increase KV read traffic and pressure on routing which amplifies queue growth.

maya: so two probs: 1) autoscaler can't add capacity due to cloud quota/rate limits 2) batching/prefix cache config change increased load and lowered throughput per GPU. both together = queue spiral.

derek: immediate mitigation options: 1) revert continuous-batching:v2 rollout -> roll back config 2) bump autoscaler max_nodes and request quota emergency increase 3) temporarily route eu-west-2 traffic to eu-central (failover) 4) increase prefix_cache ttl to previous values

maya: doing quick wins first: rolling back the rollout and scaling pool manually. @infra-bot start pool-scale job for gpu-pool-eu-west-2 +4 nodes (manual)

infra-bot: Received request to scale gpu-pool-eu-west-2 by +4 nodes. Job queued. ETA for new nodes ~4m (subject to provider rate limits).

omar: i'll open a rollback PR for continuous-batching:v2 -> revert to v1 config and link it here.

omar: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-configs/pull/893 (rollback continuous-batching-v2)

customer-support: escalating to CS lead. affected customers: acme-health, finlytics, talkdesk-prod. Opening incident status page and setting expected ETA for partial mitigation 15 min.

ops-sre: scale job started but provider returning 429s on node create; retrying with backoff. manual bump to autoscaler max_nodes needed if quota approved.

maya: @lee you’re next oncall in 10m, handing off after we confirm rollback status. current severity: SLO-impacting across region, P1-amber.

lee: acknowledged, monitoring. ask if we should preemptively drain non-critical workloads in that pool to free capacity?

maya: good idea — derek, can you tag some internal dev pools and drain non-prod jobs from this pool so new cores target prod requests?

eng-runtime: there is a hotfix we can try if rollback takes too long: adjust batch_window_ms back to 80 and prefix_cache.ttl_ms to 10000 via feature flag. That avoids full rollback of image.

maya: do the feature-flag patch then — faster. omar, please coordinate the patch and infra patch apply.

omar: applying flag change now. command: 
```
kubectl -n serving set env deployment/serving-config FEATURE_CONTINUOUS_BATCHING=off && kubectl apply -f ff/continuous-batching-rollback.yaml
```

infra-bot: Feature-flag apply acknowledged. Rolling restart of serving-config deployment.

ops-sre: provider continues to rate-limit node creations but retries succeeding slowly; pool scaled +2 so far.

eng-runtime: prefix-cache hitrate recovering to ~90% after flag flip. latency dropping on tail.

customer-support: posted interim status to status.redwood.com: "Partial mitigation in progress. Routing and config rollback underway. Customers may see intermittent 5xx in eu-west-2."

maya: tracking mitigation checklist: 
- [x] acknowledge pager and notify stakeholders
- [x] identify root cause (batching/prefix cache + quota)
- [x] apply fast rollback via feature flag (eng-runtime)
- [x] scale pool manually +2 (infra)
- [ ] confirm full rollback (PR merged) and scale to desired capacity (+4)
- [ ] request quota increase with cloud provider and follow up with sales if needed

lee: taking over primary watch. maya will remain on thread for context. i'll update on status every 5m until fully mitigated.

maya: handing off now to @lee :hand: — good run team. please keep notes in the incident doc /incidents/4765000001 postmortem.

ops-sre: final note: root cause likely a combo — config regression that increased cache missstorms and our autoscaler/quotas not having headroom for a rapid spike. recommend adding pre-deploy canary for batching changes and an autoscaler soft-headroom policy.

eng-runtime: agree. will add e2e perf check for prefix-cache hitrate on future rollout gates.

customer-support: will follow up with each affected customer with timeline and mitigations.

pagerbot: Incident acknowledged by oncall lee. Incident status: mitigated->partial. Next steps: followup postmortem, customer RCA, quota request. :thumbsup:
